title: Replacing Huey Smith with Shirley and Lee
summary: He took Huey Smith's place on the road with Shirley and Lee; he praises Huey's authentic influence.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Were there a lot of other musicians that, well, a lot of other people who have gone on to be great New Orleans musicians there at the time, attracted by the marching band? A few, a few, I'd say, but not super, super lucky with me. Was one of your first gigs playing with Shirley and Lee on the road alternating with Huey Smith?

Not alternating with it. I took Huey's place. Huey's records had begun to do very well. So it was time for him to go on his own. I went to take his place, whether it would be temporarily or permanent, and it ended up in being permanent, the first trip. So we weren't alternating, actually.
What do you think of Huey's influence on New Orleans music?

Very strong and very authentic. He's one of the true bloods of it all. He's in the studio now recording, isn't he? Well, he was a couple of months ago. He's through with that particular project. Whether he's about to start another one, I don't know. But at present, he's not in.
